writeup.headline: Booz Allen rates Hold: low valuation and solid quality offset by shrinking revenue and a leveraged balance sheet.
writeup.thesis: Booz Allen scores 55, a Hold, because its strongest factor, valuation (89), is pulled down by weak growth (23) and balance sheet (27) scores. In absolute terms the shares look low at 0.9x sales, 10.1x free cash flow and 13.7x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 4.9 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, and they are cheap against their own history, with P/FCF cheaper than at 57 of the last 61 month-ends. The business is shrinking, though, with a TTM revenue decline of 6.2% and a latest-quarter revenue decline of 3.9% year on year, even as growth sped up by 0.4 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is decent (65), with a 9.3% operating margin, a 9.0% FCF margin and diluted share count down 2.7% year on year, but net debt is 4.14 times FCF and cash covers only 0.08 of debt. News is mildly positive (62) after a raised EPS guide, analyst upgrades and a 1.5x book-to-bill, and the trend score is neutral (53).
key_risks: Continued revenue decline, including a guided low-double-digit drop in civil revenue
High leverage, with net debt at 4.14 times FCF and cash covering only 0.08 of debt
Part of the EPS guidance raise comes from one-time items, and management expects a second-half margin step-down
Dependence on U.S. government spending and contract awards
Shares down 17.1% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, with the price 18.3% below its 52-week high
what_would_change: A move to Buy needs 10 more points, most plausibly from revenue returning to growth and lifting the growth score from 23
Debt reduction that improves the balance sheet score from 27 would also help push the score up
A fall to Sell would take an 11-point drop, for example from a valuation re-rating, deeper revenue declines or negative guidance or contract news
Converting the $41B backlog into reported revenue growth would support the rating
